thread:
Alex Kim: follow-up from today's design sync: proposal for a probe-driven capability negotiation layer between edge and runtime. Goal: single /v1/infer API while preserving mode guarantees and minimizing runtime branching.
Leah Martinez: short version: runtime asks control-plane (or edge proxy) for a manifest via light probe; manifest includes capabilities, trust_level, billing_tag, manifest_id, and ttl. Signed for private.
Jon Park: how is this different from the earlier manifest idea? want to avoid duplicating effort.
Alex Kim: it's complementary. this thread focuses on the probe pattern and backpressure semantics. probe is a small HTTP GET to /v1/manifest?tenant=... that returns headers and optionally a tiny JSON body.
Maria Singh: clients shouldn't need to call probe. probes are between edge->control-plane and runtime->edge. client SDKs only adapt to capability hints emitted in responses.
Tara O'Neill: important: probes must be cheap and cacheable. runtime should probe asynchronously and keep a warm manifest. on cold start, fall back to a minimal safe manifest to avoid blocking requests.
Leah Martinez: security: signed manifests for private trust_level, include X-Manifest-Signature and X-Manifest-Key-Id. verifier caches public keys.
Jon Park: QoS: manifest includes `latency_tier` and `eviction_policy` so runtime knows to route to low-latency pools for dedicated tenants. we must avoid codepaths that branch by enum; prefer capability bits + QoS hints.
Alex Kim: agreed. runtime behavior: evaluate capabilities in priority order: 1) required features (if missing -> reject), 2) QoS hints (latency_tier -> prefer hot path), 3) billing tags (attach to telemetry). Implement decision as rule table rather than if/else tree.
Maria Singh: migration: keep /hosted, /dedicated, /private for 6 months. translation proxy maps them to /v1/infer and sets X-Requested-Mode. Proxy also caches manifest per-tenant to reduce control-plane load.
Tara O'Neill: probe rate limiting: runtime probes on events: (a) tenant connect, (b) manifest TTL expiry, (c) manifest revocation signal. cap probes to 1/s per-tenant and burst up to 5. edge should reject excessive probes.
Leah Martinez: manifest revocation: control-plane will emit a lightweight `revocations` webhook stream and set `revocation_id` in headers so runtimes can evict. Also include `manifest_version` and `issued_at`.
Jon Park: telemetry: emit metrics `manifest.latency_tier`, `manifest.fallback_count`, `manifest.verification_failures`, and tag by tenant and region. alert if fallback_count / requests > 0.5% over 5m.
Alex Kim: billing: manifest must include `billing_tag`. If runtime falls back to compatibility mode, billing tag still used but annotate `billing_note=fallback`. Billing will reject invoices with mismatched tags.
Maria Singh: DevEx will ship an SDK helper that reads `X-Redwood-Capabilities` and adjusts client behavior (e.g., enable chunked streaming if streaming=true). It should also surface warnings when behavior is degraded.
Tara O'Neill: ops: proxy rollout plan: 1) internal-only, 2) per-region feature flag, 3) opt-in tenants, 4) global. Deprecation timeline: 6 months with 30/14/7 telemetry warnings.
Leah Martinez: edge-case: on-prem tenants with slow control-plane connectivity. Support tenant-anchored keyrings and local signing (tenant_sigs) and allow longer TTLs with explicit operator approval.
Jon Park: risks: manifest churn can cause cache thrash. enforce control-plane rate limits and runtime backoff. Add manifest update smoothing: apply new manifest only if `manifest_id` changed and stable for 2s.
Alex Kim: next steps: I'll open a short RFC PR with manifest shape, probe API, and rule-table pseudo-code. Leah: include signing spec. Jon: add metrics/alerts. Maria/Tara: migration + rollout docs.
Leah Martinez: scheduling follow-up: Arch sync 2026-05-18 15:00 UTC.
Alex Kim: thanks all. Ill open the RFC today: https://git.redwood/infra/rfcs/pulls/489
Maria Singh: on review.
Jon Park: will add metric names after PR.
Tara O'Neill: will draft proxy config snippets.
